Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. We can absolutely deliver a short runbook + role matrix draft. Quick answers up front:
- Required SAML attributes: email (primary), name (displayName), groups (full group path if available). We recommend also passing a stable opaque id (redwood_subject or sub) if your IdP supports it to avoid issues when emails change.
- SCIM: we support group and user provisioning; nested groups are flattened on import but we preserve membership paths in an attribute so you can reconstruct mapping on your side.
- Service accounts: recommend using IdP-managed machine/service identities where possible. For short-lived operator sessions, we support time-limited delegated tokens; these are issued by the PrivCP control plane and show up in audit as "delegated: <idp_principal>" with the operator role.
- Certification cadence: quarterly is reasonable; initial pilot we usually do a 30-day review to validate mappings, then move to quarterly attestation.

To produce the runbook and CSV we need:
1) Example SAML assertion (or metadata URL) and which claim contains groups.
2) A sample of your group naming conventions and the initial list of groups/users you attached (we have that in the spreadsheet, thanks).
3) Who at Acme will be the attestation owner(s) (email) and any delegated approvers.

I can put together a draft role matrix (CSV) and a one-page runbook. Laura — can you take lead on the role mappings? Karthik — please flag any PrivCP operator constraints (max session time, audit label schema) that we need to surface. Ben — FYI on procurement timelines; Alice included procurement on the original.

Folks — I started a draft role matrix and attached a CSV with suggested mappings based on typical enterprise patterns. Key decisions and notes:
- Base roles: viewer, operator, admin, auditor.
- Operator role should be mapped to an IdP group named either "privcp_operators" or a nested group under "platform/privcp/operators". We included both patterns in the CSV.
- For nested groups we include an attribution column (source_group_path) so tooling can reconcile membership if Acme flattens names on SCIM import.
- Service accounts: recommend prefix "svc_" and include an attribute scim:serviceAccount=true. PrivCP will treat any principal with that attribute as non-human and apply different expiry/attestation rules.
- Audit labels: we propose audit.principal_source (idp|scim|local), audit.principal_id (opaque id if present), audit.role_binding_id. This makes certification reports deterministic.

Attachments: privcp-proposed-role-matrix.csv (text/csv)

Happy to walk through the mapping in the sync. Karthik: anything to add on session limits or token formats?

Adding a couple of operational constraints to call out before the sync:
- Max delegated operator session: configurable, default 8 hours. For high-risk tenants we suggest 1 hour with reauth.
- SCIM delta ops: we support incremental syncs every 5 minutes; if you need near real-time, we can support event-driven SCIM but that is a separate onboarding step.
- JIT provisioning: Supported for SAML assertions where the IdP sends the full set of attributes. JIT users get a "pending" state until they are first-assigned a role; we can auto-assign based on group membership.
- Token audit retention: audit events are retained for 180 days by default on Dedicated; Private (on-prem) customers can set retention via config (we recommend >=90 days for compliance).

I attached a small text file showing the sample SAML assertion elements we expect.
